title: Three Weeks of Qwikster, and the Morning Netflix Took It Back
industry: media (film and television rental and streaming)
conflicts: Q3 2011 subscriber loss: 800,000 (HuffPost and most reports) vs 810,000 net (Home Media Magazine, apparently the letter's exact figure); story gives about 800,000 and names the 810,000 count. September forecast: about 600,000 loss (Next TV) vs 'cut estimate by 1 million' (CBS), consistent. Pre-July share price: near $300 (CBS) vs 52-week high about $324 (HuffPost); story says near $300. Reversal-day share move: up about 10% in the morning (ABC) vs down almost 7% by late afternoon (CBS); left out. HuffPost dates the price split to June, other sources July; story uses July.
notes: Netflix's 2011 blog posts now redirect to its newsroom, so Wayback Machine copies are cited. The subscriber loss came in the quarter before the reversal, and the story says so. The No Rules Rules point is cited via Next TV's report of the book.
